transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m… having a hard time at work. I’m a barber, and I’ve gotten pretty bad about avoiding using the straight razor. I’ll switch clients or make excuses, even hide it sometimes. And if I can’t get out of it, I’m shaking through the shave.
Are you afraid of the straight razor itself?

Yeah… I guess so. I know it’s just a tool, and I was trained on it. I can use clippers fine all day. But when the straight razor is open there at my station, it just feels like… I’m about to cut myself badly, or hurt somebody.
Are you afraid only when you have to use the straight razor?

Not only when I’m actually using it. Even if a client just asks for a razor shave, or I see it opened up, I… my chest tightens, my hands get sweaty. It’s like I want to step back before I even really think about it.
Outside of anything involving the straight razor, do you have this same kind of fear in other parts of your life?

No… not really. It’s mostly that razor. I mean, I know it’s just a tool, I trained with it, and I can use clippers all day fine. But when the straight razor is sitting open at my station, it feels like I’m going to cut myself badly or hurt somebody.
When this fear comes up, do you get unwanted thoughts that keep repeating in your mind about cutting yourself or someone else?
I don’t know… not really like repeating over and over. It’s more like a quick thought that something bad could happen, and then I just want to get away from it.
When that fear comes up, do you feel like you have to do anything specific to make the thought go away or keep something bad from happening?
Not really. I mean… I might just close it or move away from it, but it’s not like there’s some exact thing I have to do in my head or anything.
